en: Title: *Narakoddhārastava* (Hymn for Deliverance from Hell) Author: Nāgārjuna Source:
Lindtner 1979, collated with Tokyo University Library MS No. 205 [A]; also cf. CUL MS Or.716.2.
Oṃ, homage to the Lord of the World!
Sunk in the mire of poverty within the great ocean of saṃsāra—
[of one] stuck in the mire of poverty.
Having produced full comprehension, save me, O Tathāgata!
[I am] like one who has entered a house of cataracts, experiencing the suffering of being without a protector.
I have entered the house of darkness;
abandoned by my circle of kinsmen and suffering the pain of being without a protector, save me, O Tathāgata! 2.
I have been abandoned by my circle of kinsmen—
mother, father, sister, as well as sons, wife, and friends;
indeed, even mother, father, and sister [have left me].
My sons, wife, and friends were seen by me as a magical illusion; O Tathāgata, save me!
I have seen them as consisting of a magical illusion.
Whatever wholesome or unwholesome deed I have performed for the sake of my attendants—
for the sake of my attendants.
I shall go alone; save me, O Tathāgata!
I am being cooked in a most terrible, unfathomable ocean of a ruined well.
And in the unfathomable oceans, I have become blind, O Lord; save me, O Tathāgata!
We...
I have seen myself boarded upon a dilapidated boat for the crossing of the great ocean—an ocean difficult to cross. Save me, O Tathāgata! 6.
Dharma and adharma were not understood; what may be approached and what may not be approached was not known.
This wood is insentient; O Tathāgata, protect me!
I have committed the five acts of immediate retribution, including the murder of my mother and the murder of my father; I am being cooked in the terrible darkness of hell—save me, O Tathāgata! 8.
I have caused the destruction of a stūpa,
and I have ruined the property belonging to the Saṃgha.
I have committed violence against sentient beings; O Tathāgata, protect me!
There is no happiness in this world, nor is it to be found in the next world. [In this world...]
Even while in happiness, the next world is not known; I am bound by the thread of karma—save me, O Tathāgata! 10
Just as a kāśī flower wanders in the sky, driven by the wind—such indeed is this life; protect me, O Tathāgata! 11
Such was his [laughter]. Indeed.
The forest is overgrown with thorns and lacks refuge among its many trees;
the path is indeed full of thorns, and I see no way through it—save me, O Tathāgata! 12.
There was no path there;
innocent animals and deer were struck by me with arrows.
"Though innocent, Vasu was killed; many deer were slain by hunters. 'I am a king,' I thought then—do not think so! Save me, O Tathāgata! (13)
The king said: "I think that for one being cooked in hell, there will be some savior;
yet, [even while] being cooked..."
No protector is found anywhere.
To whom shall I go for refuge? Who will be my savior?
You are the king of physicians among physicians, the healer of all diseases.
But you, O King of Physicians, [are the one who] heals all diseases; O Lord of the World, become a savior for the three worlds, including all that is mobile and immobile. || 15 ||
May he become a protector of the world.
[End of the *Narakoddharaṇastava*.]
Ye dharmā...

This religious gift belongs to the supreme Mahāyāna follower, the eminent female lay devotee (paramopāsikā), the illustrious Śrīramālavadhū, daughter of the Māṇḍalika Śrī [and] named Sūhava; whatever merit there is herein...
